consistency_checks.detail: SBP 146 mmHg directly supports essential hypertension diagnosis.
HDL 28 mg/dL meets one criterion for metabolic syndrome; other criteria partially met.
HbA1c 5.9% reflects prediabetes, supporting insulin‑resistance component.
High‑normal hematocrit and modest RBC reduction are atypical for iron deficiency; suggests anemia of chronic disease may be more likely.
BUN alone cannot confirm CKD; missing creatinine/eGFR leaves early CKD diagnosis unsupported.

top_concerns: Primary diagnosis ranking places iron‑deficiency anemia above untreated hypertension
Overestimation of iron‑deficiency anemia without iron studies
Absence of renal function labs limits assessment of CKD
Missing iron panel, ferritin, and stool occult blood to clarify anemia etiology
Incomplete metabolic work‑up (triglycerides, waist circumference) for metabolic syndrome
review_summary: The junior differential captures most relevant issues but mis‑ranks the most actionable problem. Hypertension is strongly supported and should be the primary focus. Several diagnoses (iron‑deficiency anemia, early CKD, OSA) are over‑estimated given missing confirmatory data. Additional labs (iron studies, renal panel, full lipid profile, TSH, vitamin D) and targeted screenings (depression, sleep apnea) are needed to refine the differential.
